When the preflight door KILLs a guard, it deletes the guard's own TMPDIR (1600-nn5b) but not .tillandsias/fixture-scratch/<guard>.<pid>, the per-run scratch subdir that repo-confined fixtures use since 1611-imnj. A fixture killed at the deadline leaves that subdir behind.

methodology/multi-host-development.yaml tells hosts to "prefer separate `git worktree` directories" for concurrent work. Hosts do, and each sibling worktree sits outside the session's workspace. The command-policy bridge then asks the OPERATOR to approve any recursive rm there, and one shared cargo target mixes checkouts. The operator's direction: one checkout per repo, with work moved between branches by `git switch`.

bash_policy.rs context_for() counts /tmp, /private/tmp and the session's TMPDIR as scratch roots. On darwin, an agent session's TMPDIR can be elsewhere (here /private/tmp/claude-501/...), and the OS's own per-user temp dir (getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR, /var/folders/<..>/T/) is not one. So a recursive rm of scratch that bare mktemp leaked there is consent:bash-policy:workspace-destroy, put to the OPERATOR.

When a lane exits while ANOTHER project's lane is up, cleanup_shared_stack_if_no_running_forge returns at "keeping shared stack alive; active lane container(s): ..." before any per-project cleanup. The exiting project's tillandsias-git-<project> mirror keeps running after its last lane, and the sibling's later exit cleans only its own project, so the mirror leaks until some future cold launch.

A lane launch for a project whose local branch (master) does not exist upstream (default main) waits in wait_for_git_mirror_ready for refs/heads/master. The wait runs the full GIT_MIRROR_COLD_SEED_MAX_WAIT_SECS (20 min), and every attempt says "HEAD resolvable but expected branch refs/heads/master is not concrete yet - seed still in progress". The ref can never appear, so the operator waits twenty minutes on a misdiagnosis.

scripts/lua/check-shell-ratchet.lua refuses a new piped litmus `command:` (violation:shell-ratchet:new-piped-command) only inside `if n_steps > 0`, i.e. only once some litmus file uses the steps: form. No real litmus file does (litmus-form:...:steps=0). On the real tree the LITMUS arm is therefore dormant and answers ok at every head, while the gate's fixture scripts/lua/test-shell-ratchet.lua seeds a steps: file, wakes the arm, and refuses the same tree. Authors see green locally, and the land queue evicts.

A user should start a web project in a forge from a Tillandsias template: the default is a plain static site served by wrangler (no build step); Flutter + Flame is an opt-in template. Templates carry the local-preview wiring, so "launch this project locally" works with no setup.

An opt-in sibling Flutter image (the same pattern as the Wrangler preview image) should build `flutter build web` for a forge project, with Flame from pub.dev, and its output preview through publish_local.

A project previewed in a forge should deploy from the same build image: a GitHub Actions workflow template runs the image's build and `wrangler deploy`, reading a Cloudflare token from a GitHub secret. No Cloudflare credential ever enters a forge.

The chromium-framework browser container gets the host's whole $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR read-write on Wayland: the podman socket (host code execution), the tray control socket, the D-Bus session bus and the keyring. On X11 it gets all of /tmp/.X11-unix read-write, and X11 wins whenever DISPLAY is set. The container also runs with --security-opt=label=disable. It must mount only the Wayland socket file, Wayland only.
The darwin-background preflight door overruns its 450 s budget (452 s, then 909 s), so the budget is not the bound on the door's wall time it claims to be
The macOS install's SOFT reset kept a VM damaged by a force-stop, and its guest SIGBUS-crashed into a dead login and forge; build a fresh VM on every install and carry only identity forward

A vendored device catalogue plus a resolver: "iphone", "iphone 12", "iphone 12 pro", "iphone 12 pro max", "galaxy s24 ultra", "xperia", "oneplus 12" and "desktop" each resolve to the right fixed viewport, screen, dpr, engine and UA. Exposed as `tillandsias devices resolve <query>`.

Grow the device catalogue (1643-q3at, 127 devices) to the long tail the operator asked for: hundreds of KB covering many brands, so a mobile-first preview can be checked on the phones people actually hold.

accel_envelope maps ANY container-usable GPU to accel_class=workstation-gpu, and lib-common.sh tells every forge agent that class means "a discrete GPU is deliverable to this container — larger models are cheap here"; an integrated GPU (measured: a WSL2 AMD Radeon 860M iGPU over Mesa Dozen, non-conformant Vulkan 1.2) then oversells and an agent picks too large a model
793-a8e7 S2: on the opted-in gpu-vulkan lane the accel probe judges the WSL2 dxg GPU from inside the inference container (vulkaninfo --summary), so the opted-in lane stops reporting cpu-only

793-a8e7 S3: on the opted-in lane, models below the decode floor are pinned all-CPU (num_gpu 0) at container start and restored on opt-out with no residue; the floor is the measured crossover, else 3B provisional

On macOS VZ the Fedora guest kernel stalls after systemd-shutdown's "Powering off.", so VZ stays Running and only a host stop ends the VM

Development mode: browser.open{dev:true} gives the lane that opened the window full browser control (typed navigate/evaluate/console-tail/network-tail/screenshot/emulate tools plus raw browser.cdp{window_id, method, params, sessionId?}) over its peer-authenticated per-lane MCP socket. Other lanes get WINDOW_NOT_FOUND. There is no host TCP listener and no wider network than a normal window.

A WebKit engine container built from Playwright's Linux WebKit (WebKit LGPL/BSD, Playwright Apache-2.0) opens Apple presets (engine webkit in the device catalogue), on Wayland only with the same per-window network as Chromium. It is labelled "WebKit (approximates Safari)" everywhere it is named.

The typed dev-mode tools (navigate, evaluate, console and network tails, screenshot, emulate, set_device) work the same on a Chromium window (CDP) and a WebKit window (the Playwright protocol). Raw browser.cdp on a WebKit window returns a typed ENGINE_UNSUPPORTED error naming the engine, never a hang or a CDP-shaped lie.

On macOS, browser.open shows the Chromium (or WebKit) container from the tray's Linux VM in its own Mac window. The VM gets a VZVirtioGraphicsDeviceConfiguration display; a cage Wayland kiosk in the guest runs the browser; the guest display and the VZVirtualMachineView are sized to the device's CSS viewport, one view per window.

The Safari appliance: an opt-in, separate macOS guest VM (not the tray's Linux VM) running Safari and the iOS Simulator, driven by safaridriver (W3C WebDriver) with safari:useSimulator for iOS presets. A forwarder in the guest reaches the host router; the router CA lives only in the guest keychain. It is off by default on floor-tier Macs.

Windows NPU inference helper: a host-side, inference-only server confined in an AppContainer (MXC processcontainer or equivalent) with all egress denied, serving one socket or named pipe that the WSL2 enclave reaches through the tray. This is the Windows slice of 483, and the counterpart of the macOS Metal helper (1654-6me6).

The tillandsias-chromium-framework image has no fonts (a TODO), so pages render with missing or tofu glyphs. No fixture pins the image entrypoint's refusal of --no-sandbox (612-nvf3), so a regression that re-admits it would pass every gate.

Two cheatsheet errors: cheatsheets/runtime/wslg-chromium-passthrough.md and wsl-browser-isolation.md recommend --use-angle=d3d11 for Chromium inside WSL2, but ANGLE's d3d11 backend exists only in Windows builds of Chromium; cheatsheets/runtime/macos-vz-gui-research-v2.md (and its copy under images/default/cheatsheets/) says Virtualization.framework has no virtio-gpu, but VZVirtioGraphicsDeviceConfiguration serves Linux guests since macOS 13.
browser.open runs the chromium-framework container, never host Chromium, and admits the local preview port.

./build.sh --preflight on a Windows checkout left a stale 0-byte .git/index.lock in BOTH runs on 2026-10-12 (created mid-run, no git process alive afterwards), and the lock then refused the next git add and git switch; the likely cause is a guard killed at the 5 s front-door deadline while inside a git index write
A browser.open window can reach only its own project: a per-window SNI-bound forwarder replaces the router on the window's network, and the router enforces Host == SNI.
A device query that only a model with an EXTRA modifier token matches (galaxy s23 → Galaxy S23 FE) must resolve approximated, naming that model, never exact.
Mac GPU route decision record — libkrun/krunkit Venus Vulkan inside the VM vs Metal on the host
macOS Metal inference helper: a Seatbelt-confined host llama-server with no network, serving one Unix socket that the VM's enclave reaches over vsock through the tray
browser.open{url, device?} opens the container window at the device's fixed size with CDP device emulation, and browser.set_device switches it live.

browser.open's container window works on Windows through WSLg: the owned Fedora 44 WSL2 guest hands the chromium-framework container only the WSLg Wayland socket file, on the same per-window internal network as Linux

The landing queue's WORK_RE (work/[0-9]{3,4}-[a-z0-9]{4}) admits only suffixed orders, so a row whose order predates the four-character suffix (539, 472, and 17 ready rows from 151 to 554) has NO ref name the queue will land, and the queue's skip comment names a grammar the author cannot satisfy.

A dev-mode browser window offers the lane that opened it a raw CDP socket under that lane's /run/host/tillandsias-mcp/, so Playwright or Puppeteer inside the forge can drive the window directly. No other lane sees it, and the host gains no TCP listener.
The macOS installation anchor, which the in-VM Vault derives its master key from, is minted from the wall clock and the pid instead of the OS RNG
The Vault partial-init guard concludes "no share" before the host's credential delivery can arrive, and wipes a valid store
A WebKit window's OS title names its engine, "WebKit (approximates Safari)", next to the page title. Users see the title bar, not the MCP tool results.

Workload identity plane: every enclave workload is named in SPIFFE form, every enclave connection authenticates both ends, and every lane is SELinux-confined to its own category
Any enclave container can push to the git mirror over anonymous git:// and the privileged relay carries it to GitHub under the operator's identity; the SSH-CA lane must be the only receive path
One SPIFFE-form name for every enclave workload — spiffe://<host-trust-domain>/project/<mirror-id>/lane/<instance>[/agent/<harness>] — carried in the SSH lane cert's Key ID

Every forge commit carries a workload-identity trailer (project, lane, agent harness, model) that the mirror can verify but that cannot be aggregated across projects, signed with the lane's short-lived SSH cert

A guard enumerates every enclave listener (vault, mirror git and ssh, router, proxy, inference, per-lane sockets, browser forwarder, web preview, expert-serve) with its client-auth mode, and any listener with client-auth=none fails unless it carries a named, dated waiver
Vault requires a lane client certificate (1 h, URI SAN = the lane's SPIFFE ID, minted by the existing sidecar) in addition to the AppRole token, so a stolen token alone reads nothing
inference:11434 trusts anything on the enclave network; put a TLS-terminating front that requires an enclave lane client cert in front of every inference engine, on all three platforms

The router and the egress proxy trust source IP and network placement; each must authenticate the calling lane by its enclave client cert, so per-project routing and egress policy key on identity, not address

The ssh-agent sidecar socket and the per-lane control/MCP socket trust whoever can open the file; each must check the peer with SO_PEERCRED and its cgroup against the owning lane's container id (SPIRE's unix + docker workload attestation, without SPIRE)

--security-opt=label=disable is one of the four MANDATORY_HARDENING_FLAGS, so every enclave container runs SELinux-unconfined and any other label= is refused as a weakening; invert it so container_t with a per-container MCS pair is the default and label=disable is a named, justified exception

Per-lane sockets are SELinux-confined: each socket file carries its lane container's MCS pair so only that lane can connectto it, and the forge, mirror, router and proxy get confined types (udica/CIL, following vault_container_t) that allow only their own sockets and ports
Cross-host trust for the fleet mesh and inference swarm: each host publishes its enclave-CA bundle in SPIFFE federation form, and peers trust a listed domain one-way without ever merging bundles

Every successful host-browser tool call (publish_local, service_status, service_reload, browser_open, browser_list_windows) reaches the agent empty, because success results are a bare JSON object with no MCP content array; only errors are wrapped

A forge agent cannot tell which Tillandsias release its host runs: no tillandsias binary on PATH, nothing in .forge-startup-context.md, no env var; expose TILLANDSIAS_HOST_VERSION and a host_version= line in the startup context

A link that leaves the app's preview (linkedin.com, tillandsias.org, another project) shows a small toast in the same device window, worded for non-technical users, with a split [Open ▾] button whose last-used choice is preselected; the choices come from an extensible registry

Release cut section 8 for v56.10.14.1: README ledger rows (v56.10.14.1, and v56.10.13.1, which had none), work-queue lines, and the observatorium release snapshot

On Windows, "serve this project locally and open it as an iPhone 16" works end to end: publish_local in the guest plus browser.open{device:"iphone 16"} opens a container window through WSLg

WSLg's two-way clipboard between container windows and Windows is audited, and the tradeoff is stated in the tillandsias.org security promises
The owned WSL2 guest runs with drive automount and Windows interop off wherever the forge does not need them, so a container window cannot reach Windows files or start Windows programs
Investigate a streamed container display (KasmVNC/noVNC style) as an opt-in safety layer for users who will pay its cost over WSLg

In an empty project, a forge agent asked how to start a new project runs an end-user onboarding skill: it asks to use spec-driven development with OpenSpec, strongly suggests Flutter (plus Flame for graphics apps), initializes specs and a ./plan path for long-running work, in plain words with no Tillandsias internals, on Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex

The prompt-to-app path starts from a brand-new GitHub repo with no commits; nobody has verified that the tray lists it, the mirror clones an unborn branch, the forge starts, and the first commit pushes back through the relay to GitHub

Design: after "push to remote", Cloudflare builds and serves the project on the user's own Cloudflare domain with no dashboard clicks; decide between Workers Builds (connected to the GitHub repo) and a GitHub Actions workflow with a token secret, and how the repo, the build and the custom domain get wired from Tillandsias

litmus check-log-survives-the-cache-sweep FAILs in every worktree under target/work: its `*/target/*` case matches the worktree's own path, contradicting the scratch-location direction that puts development worktrees there

In a forge launched through the macOS tray (v56.10.14.1), host-browser fails with CONNECTION_CLOSED: /run/host/tillandsias-mcp is mounted with TILLANDSIAS_CONTROL_SOCKET set, but the directory is empty, so no mcp.sock exists. Source read: the in-VM guest binary is built with `--features listen-vsock` (build-macos-tray.sh, build-guest-binaries.sh, flake), and start_mcp_socket_server_for_lane lives in tray/mod.rs behind #[cfg(feature = "tray")], so the guest mounts the lane dir and never binds the listener. Every host-browser tool (publish_local, service_status, service_reload, browser_open, browser_list_windows, the dev-mode CDP tools) is unreachable from macOS forges, and by the same build, likely from Windows forges too.

The forge egress proxy refuses a project's own deployed public domain, so an agent can't load the site it just pushed: it can't measure push → live or check that the deploy serves what it built. Admit read-only GET and HEAD to exactly the domains the project itself declares (its wrangler routes and custom_domain entries), for that project's forge only. This is never a general opening.

A FROM line pinned to a single-platform digest builds an image for the wrong architecture, and nothing fails: the macOS tray VM (aarch64 Fedora) has a qemu-x86_64 binfmt handler, so an amd64-only base runs emulated and labelled arm64. Every `FROM …@sha256:` must be a multi-arch index digest, and a guard over all FROM lines must refuse a single-platform one.

A dev build of the macOS tray (scripts/build-macos-tray.sh, or a target/ binary) runs against the SAME state as the installed /Applications/Tillandsias.app: the VM image root (~/Library/Application Support/tillandsias: rootfs.img, vm-identity.img, swap, console.log, unclean-rebuilds.log), the staged guest binary and its provenance sidecar (~/.local/state/tillandsias/guest-bin), the Keychain items (vault-shamir-share-v1, vault-root-token-v1, tillandsias-vm-uuid), and the guest's vsock CID. A dev build must use its own VM home and state, chosen by what the binary IS (a dev or unsigned build), so it can never touch the installed tray's VM or sign-ins.

`tillandsias --cloudflare-login` can't complete on any account. CLOUDFLARE_APP_CLIENT_ID is still the placeholder "tillandsias-cloudflare-app-client-id-unregistered", and CLOUDFLARE_LOGIN_SCOPES is empty. MEASURED: an authorize request with no scope makes Cloudflare's consent screen ask for "0 total permissions", with Authorize disabled. The operator has now registered the Tillandsias OAuth client (client id d9d1303782dfe45c7e2d7bb9ce89c8a8, public, like GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_ID), and Cloudflare's scope ids are dotted and hyphenated (workers-ci.write), not wrangler's colon form.

No tray (macOS, Windows or Linux) has a "Cloudflare Login" item, although design Decision 7 called for one, so a user has no way to run `tillandsias --cloudflare-login` from the app. Add it, mirroring GitHub Login: a shared menu row, visible only while no Cloudflare bundle is stored, that opens a terminal on the VM running `tillandsias-headless --cloudflare-login` (paste mode in the guest, which has no browser opener).

Cloudflare's discovery document now lists the device-code grant (urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code, with a device_authorization_endpoint), which the 1505 design assumed did not exist. If Cloudflare grants it to the Tillandsias client, the login can work like `--github-login`: a short code to approve on any device (phone included), with no redirect, no 127.0.0.1 page and nothing to paste. That's the frictionless path the operator asked for.
UX review: the operator gates and regroups every tray menu item on all three platforms; until it lands, new items (Cloudflare Login, 1719-83po) are placed provisionally

The guest's exec allowlist (exec_allowlist.rs) admits `/bin/bash -lc <any script>` and, via the 795-zshi verbatim arm, ANY absolute program with ANY arguments, so it constrains nothing that matters. Whether that is acceptable depends on one unmeasured fact: can anything other than the host tray open a connection to the guest's control listener (vsock port 42420)? From the host, only the VM's owner process can. From inside the guest, a forge container might, through vsock loopback, and the channel PSK would not stop it, because it is derived from the hash of a public release binary.

Two guards that make 1721-fcm0's single barrier not single. (1) The tillandsias-vsock-forwarder bridges `inference:11434`, which every forge reaches by design, to VSOCK-CONNECT:{cid}:{port}, and nothing validates the target. A target of (1, 42420) would bridge every forge to the guest's control listener. The guest must refuse any forward target unless cid == 2 (VMADDR_CID_HOST) and port != 42420 (CONTROL_WIRE_VSOCK_PORT), from EVERY source. (2) A forge can't open AF_VSOCK only because of containers-common's default seccomp rule; a litmus must fail if any forge launch carries a seccomp override or --privileged.
A game playing in a host-browser window is silent: the browser container has no route to the host's sound server, so audio Chromium produces never reaches the speakers

service_reload {category: WEB} fails with "runtime_unavailable: podman failed at step run (timeout)", and service_status reports nothing afterwards, so nobody knows whether the preview picked up the rebuilt bundle
Forge agents keep killing their own shell with pkill -f (exit 144): the pattern matches the agent's own command line. The forge's agent guidance must say to use pgrep and kill by PID, skipping $$

Every forge launch writes .forge-startup-context.md (images/default/lib-common.sh inject_startup_context), but only OpenCode is pointed at it (opencode agent/status.md, instructions/*). Nothing tells a Claude or Codex forge agent the file exists, so those agents never see experts_state, the accel envelope, web_publish_state/web_publish_reason (1664-finm), the host release (1701-ze9y), or, in a Tillandsias forge, the push-before-exit gate. Each harness must receive it.

A preview window kept showing the FIRST build after the preview died, because the app's service worker served it from cache; the user read that as "hot reload doesn't work". Dev windows must bypass service workers by default (and say so), and a dead preview must be visible as dead

A project's own browser tests (Playwright and the like) cannot install a browser in a forge, because cdn.playwright.dev and playwright.download.prss.microsoft.com are blocked; the agent had to hand-download Chrome for Testing from storage.googleapis.com. Ship a pinned headless shell and export its path, or admit those hosts

Design: a real iPhone cannot reach a forge's preview (https://www.<project>.localhost:18443 is the host's loopback), so today every real-device test is a production deploy. Choose the path for phones on the user's LAN or account to reach a live preview

Live reload for any stack: when a project's build output changes, every preview window the lane opened reloads (or swaps CSS), so a TypeScript/WASM project gets the edit-and-see loop that Flutter gets from its own hot reload

The forge's RAM checkout (256-348 MB tmpfs) breaks any real web or Rust project: the agent had to move node_modules, .cache, target and TMPDIR onto ~/.cache/tillandsias-project by hand before ./build.sh --dev would run. Heavy build directories should land on the persistent cache volume automatically

A Flutter web build that an agent publishes with publish_local and opens with browser.open never starts. By default the engine loads CanvasKit from www.gstatic.com, and a browser.open window resolves only its project's hosts. The forge's `flutter build web` should default to --no-web-resources-cdn, so a locally previewed build behaves like the dev server (fixed for `flutter run -d web-server` in 1637-5765) and like the deployed site.

A browser.open window's FIRST navigation can lose its subresources to net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED. Chromium aborts in-flight requests while the freshly started window's network settles. window_cdp::navigate retries only the document (1656-iktu), so a multi-asset page opens half-loaded with no error to the agent: a Flutter app never boots, and any SPA misses its bundle. Single-HTML pages never show it.
A browser window in the WSL2 guest has no sound; WSLg serves PulseAudio at /mnt/wslg/PulseServer, which also allows recording, so it needs the same output-only front end as Linux before any mount
Orchestration optimization: land more PRs per gate, catch bounce causes before a gate, let peers own their PRs, and stop micro-managing peers, measured against the 2026-10-15 baseline

The land queue gates every PR alone (~17-35 min each, serially), so a 4-PR run costs 4 gates; stack the ready candidates into one merge train, gate once, land them all on green, and bisect only when the train is red

./build.sh --preflight passed for PRs the land queue then bounced: a missing Carried-Waiver trailer (3 on 2026-10-15), the combined tray,listen-vsock test set (1), a non-work-ref branch (1). Preflight must run the same cheap checks

The queue fixes its candidate list at launch, so a PR made draft mid-run was still gated and landed (#427). Collisions between sibling PRs (#432/#433, #433/#436) surface only at merge. Re-read draft status per candidate, and post an overlap advisory when two open PRs touch the same files

Every peer PR passes through the coordinator by hand (re-push yolanda's salvage ref as work/, open the PR, re-preflight). Let Windows push work/ refs on a preflight stamp, have peers open their own non-draft PRs, and drop the coordinator re-preflight for Linux peers

Methodology gains a peer autonomy charter: peers get 3-5 row queues and decide within a row's scope; they escalate only for an outward act under the operator's identity, a cross-row scope change, a security boundary, or conflicting rulings; status is one line (READY:/DONE:/BLOCKED:)

A litmus pin broken by a landed PR (#427's PASS-line rewording) reached cut time unseen, because only the release tier runs the pre-build litmus; and nothing stops writes to the checkout while the queue gates there. After each land run, run the pre-build litmus scoped to the specs the landed PRs touched; hold a lock while gating

One host's malformed fragment (depends_on naming an order) passed its own plan-lane check and then made every other host's plan push refuse; and hosts resolve different installed plan binaries (~/.local/bin is older than the checkout), so they disagree on whether the same ledger is valid

The Linux curl|bash installer still ends with `tillandsias --reset-state --debug`, the FULL reset that wipes the host-held Vault credentials, so every reinstall forces a new sign-in. The operator ruled installers SOFT-only "forever" on 2026-10-08, and the Windows and macOS installers already comply

A WebKit browser.open window maps only www.<project>.localhost and web.<project>.localhost to the forwarder, so a routed Flutter dev server at flutter.<project>.localhost (a DEV_SERVICES host since 1637-5765) does not resolve in it. The WebKit window should map the same project hosts the router serves, dev services included.

On Linux, the SOFT reset that every curl|bash install runs calls `podman system reset --force`, which destroys EVERY podman object for the user: their own images, containers, volumes and toolboxes, not only Tillandsias'. On an end user's machine that is data we do not own. The reset must remove only Tillandsias objects (by our labels, names and image repositories) and leave everything else byte-identical.

select-work-batch.sh ran the order-645 urgency override before the 1034-whsp cross-branch drop, so when a sibling held the chosen epic's p1 rows the batch offered p2 work while p1 rows were claimable; the release gate's urgency step went red on the v56.10.15.1 cut

While a Codex forge session runs, lines prefixed "[tillandsias]" are written into the agent's full-screen TUI and corrupt it until a window resize forces a redraw. Every Tillandsias log line must go to a log file or the tray, never to a terminal an agent owns

At tray start the GitHub token rotation runs before Vault is up, reports "ok:github-token-rotation:no-token", and waits the full 15-minute interval. If the access token expired meanwhile, the cloud-project list and the user probe fail for up to 15 minutes with an empty error, because the gh script swallows gh's stderr

The onboarding skill start-a-new-project is present at /opt/skills in the v56.10.15.1 forge, yet the OpenCode agent says it is not among its available skills. The onboarding release's headline feature is invisible to the agent, which blocks stable promotion

On a VM host (macOS, likely Windows) the GitHub token rotation scheduler's first due-check runs before the Vault container is up. VaultGitHubTokenStore::read_bundle answers Ok(None) when the container is not running, so the check returns NoToken silently and sleeps the full 15-minute interval. After `tillandsias-tray --opencode <path> --prompt ...` exited 0, the next tray launch logged "reset: REBUILD (unclean previous stop)" and destroyed rootfs.img, including the forge image the run had just built. On v56.10.15.1 macOS (8 vCPU / 8 GiB guest, 24 GiB disk swap plus 2 GiB zram), the forge image build failed in two of four attempts on a clean disk. msg_recv, msg_status and msg_send in images/default/config-overlay/mcp/forge-plan.sh answer only "forge-plan.sh: line 1207: : command not found" (line 1224 for msg_send) for the whole session when the forge-plan MCP server started before tillandsias-plan was installed. msg_capability_gap resolves PLAN_BIN, but its callers run it as gap="$(msg_capability_gap)", a subshell, so the resolved value never reaches the server process and "$PLAN_BIN" stays empty.

A cold forge launch leaves TILLANDSIAS_EMBED_ENDPOINT unset even though the enclave inference service is ready, so the spec index is skipped ("[spec-index] skipped (no-embed-endpoint)") and spec_answer refuses for the whole session. lib-common.sh calls resolve_embed_endpoint with ">/dev/null 2>&1", so the probe's verdict (why it failed) is never logged, and nothing retries it when the spec-index step runs 3 minutes later.

At every forge launch on yolanda, the first lifecycle line after pull-cache is "hot-paths | FAILED: cp /opt/cheatsheets-image/. -> /opt/cheatsheets/ (cp=1): cp: preserving times for '/opt/cheatsheets/.': Operation not permitted". The failure appears nowhere the agent reads (.forge-startup-context.md has no line for it), so whether /opt/cheatsheets is complete is unknown to the agent.

The cold tillandsias-plan build in a forge logged 97 "warning: spurious network error (3 tries remaining): [16] Error in the HTTP2 framing layer" lines fetching crates through the enclave proxy. The build succeeded (184 s), but each warning is a retried download on the agent's critical path to working experts.

ensure_forge_harnesses (images/default/lib-common.sh) refreshes EVERY harness on EVERY lane: a Claude lane npm-installs @openai/codex (411 MB) and runs the Antigravity installer for agy (208 MB) on each launch. The operator expects a lane to install only its own harness. The extra work also held the npm update lock, and the Claude lane's foreground path waited 18 s on it for openspec.
A guest socket path is never resolved relative to /: an empty XDG_RUNTIME_DIR counts as unset
The Antigravity lane never reached a forge on Windows v56.10.15.1: its login container's command died after 8 s and the lane ended without saying why

seed_claude_pretooluse_hook puts `tillandsias-plan policy classify-bash --hook` into every forge's ~/.claude/settings.json "so every Claude session in a forge on ANY project has its Bash commands checked". But the forge image never ships tillandsias-plan: a forge builds it asynchronously, and only from a Tillandsias checkout's own crate. In any other project the hook's command is never found (exit 127), which Claude Code treats as a non-blocking hook error, so every rule (credential mutation, unquoted heredocs, 1724's pkill -f) is silently off

After an unclean-stop REBUILD, the macOS tray reports phase=Ready while its event is still "Securing Vault". A quit in that window drains "cleanly", but the next boot of the same guest disk fails "unseal request returned HTTP 400: wrong key" and stops at "OPERATOR ACTION REQUIRED". The tray shows Ready with the GitHub repo list at 0 entries and no error. The store itself is intact: a later REBUILD unseals it with every sign-in. Reproduced 2 of 2

When the guest Vault cannot unseal and stops at "OPERATOR ACTION REQUIRED", the macOS tray still shows phase=Ready, the GitHub repo list goes to "(0 entries)", and nothing in the tray or its log says Vault is down. A user sees a working app with no repos and no reason, and the obvious response (sign in again) cannot help

On darwin, `./build.sh --preflight` exits 133 (SIGTRAP) once the gate roster reaches 260 guards: /bin/bash 3.2 aborts on heap corruption inside realloc entered from a signal handler. Trunk sits at 259, so the next host to add any gate step makes every Mac preflight end in a bash crash after its verdict line

A host-browser `browser.open` window opened by a one-shot agent run (`opencode run …` in a forge) is SIGKILLed about 20 s after that run exits, so the operator never sees the window the agent reported as open ("headless": false, a window_id). An interactive session keeps it alive only as long as the session lasts

The forge's push report (1264-s4id) names a GitHub BRANCH-PROTECTION refusal on the startup branch ("move away from <branch>"), which the mirror's push dry-run cannot see because --dry-run never sends a pack, so protection and pre-receive hooks never fire

The published static aarch64 headless (tillandsias-headless-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl) embeds an x86_64 router sidecar, because flake.nix has no aarch64 sidecar derivation and the aarch64 headless's preBuild stages the x86_64 one; the release's `file | grep aarch64` reads only the outer binary, so it passes. Blocks 1291-38mt (the aarch64 install path)

The QR sign-in relay (assets/cloudflare-relay/index.html, 1505-kc5f) is deployed at https://observatorium.tillandsias.org/tillandsias/cloudflare/callback with a poll endpoint at /tillandsias/cloudflare/poll, registered as a redirect URI on the Tillandsias Cloudflare app, and is the login's default, so the tray's Cloudflare Login completes from a phone scan with no env var set
